## Efficient Execution: Attention Kernels and Inference Parallelism {#sec-ch4}

::: {.callout-note title="Scaffold status"}
Scaffold only: drafting has not yet begun. This page records the approved plan for the chapter; it contains no teaching content, questions, answers, figures, worked examples or citations yet.
:::

**Purpose.** Explain what attention kernels change and what they leave unchanged, and how to place a model across devices for latency or throughput.

**Prerequisites and planned recap.** Workbook 05 Chapter 5 (FlashAttention in training) and Chapter 4 (parallelism in training); Workbook 04 Chapter 5 (MoE); Chapters 1--3 of this workbook.

**Scope boundaries.** No CUDA programming or compiler tuning. Low-precision attention is a pointer to Chapter 5 only, and no Chapter 4 question depends on it. Inference pipeline parallelism stays brief (no registered primary source). Separate prefill and decode pools are Chapter 3.

### Learning objectives

Planned outcomes (approved scope). By the end of this chapter you should be able to:

- Explain online-softmax tiling and in what sense it is mathematically equivalent to standard attention.
- Explain why a query length of one limits batch-and-head parallelism at decode, and how splitting the KV sequence addresses it.
- Keep kernel-level and end-to-end claims apart.
- Choose between replicas and tensor parallelism (and expert parallelism for MoE) for a latency or throughput goal.
- Explain why a multi-query cache saving can be lost when the single KV head is replicated under head sharding.
